title: Benny Goodman's reaction to the Swing Man arrangement, and his planned opera
summary: Goodman called Old Man River too simple a tune for such an arrangement but played Swing Man; Randolph says he is working on an opera with choreography.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: See? But it was played passable. Played passable. Just -- I don't know. I just can't get them to -- I don't know what, they just don't have time. I carried

an arrangement to Benny Goodman. And Goodman said, "Man, I'm surprised at you, writing such a tune." Now, this is the way he said it. He said, "Randolph, I'm surprised at you, writing such a simple tune as Old Man River and making an arrangement like this. See?
Well, that's what he said. But he made the introduction, he did, he really did, with the band. The rest of the band did.

And it started -- well, it was kind of funny. The title of the arrangement was "Swing Man." So the introduction started out this way, the drummer says (unintelligible), and that's what I -- I had that rhythm, because I wanted that to go that way.
And then, they're supposed to say -- then the whole band says, "See, man," and then he said, "No, Swing Man."
So when they say "Swing Man," then Benny Goodman said (unintelligible), and I had them diving and cutting, and Benny was playing. And he made it --
You wrote it all out for him.
Yeah. Well, yes, because I had some things that I wanted to go along with the arrangement.

Because if you don't, then they may have to put the ideas in and that may not be what you want to go in there. Well, he made it. And that's the way the thing go. I was just saying, I just wished I really could get things going like I want them.
I have another thing kicking around in my brain, about an opera, I want to try to get this going if I can, before I peg out.
If I can, yes. If I can get -- I might be able to get an angel agent or somebody to see about putting it on. And the choreography, I even write that.
